problem: The answer 'Axis 180° gives the meridian of the cylinder' is shorthand that students often misread. In minus-cylinder form, 180° is the meridian in which the cylinder has no power; the -0.75 D cylinder acts along 90°. As written, a student may think the cylinder power acts at 180°.
fix: Say: 'Axis 180° is the cylinder axis, the meridian along which the -0.75 D cylinder has no power. The cylinder power acts along the meridian 90° away, that is 90°.'

problem: 'Refraction is the lens power that corrects a focus error' mixes the measurement with the prescription. In clinical use, refraction is the determination of the eye's refractive state; the correcting power is written as the prescription.
fix: 'Refraction is the measurement of the eye's refractive error. The correcting lens power is written as sphere, cylinder and axis in dioptres.'

problem: 'A person can have 6/6 acuity with glasses and still need a strong prescription' is easily misread as saying the person needs a stronger prescription than the glasses they wear.
fix: 'A person wearing glasses can read 6/6 and still have a large prescription, for example -6.00 D. Acuity tells you the sharpness reached; it does not tell you the lens power.'

problem: 'in every eye clinic' overstates the claim; small or basic clinics may not have all three instruments.
fix: 'These three measurements support glaucoma screening, eye examination and spectacle prescription in a typical eye clinic.'
